purpose: Test whether the frozen Phase-1 ledgers contain source-linked evidence adequate for five bounded reasoning-process views before any view is constructed or model is called.

targets.description: The user moves from considering an immediate build to a bounded no-build discovery plan, while the assistant preserves unresolved prototype and trust risks.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: My provisional plan is to offer Northline three focused sessions over the next two weeks, document the workflow, and explicitly make no build commitment.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The two risks you named remain real: restricting prototypes may make discovery artificial, while careful language may still feel like distance to Northline.

targets.description: A time-boxed investigation with separate reliability ownership is considered, along with the failure condition that both paths cannot actually be staffed.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: One possible design is to time-box her investigation while another owner defines the minimum reliability work that cannot slip, then reconvene with actual effort and ownership.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: But if the team cannot staff both without wishful allocation, the experiment will not solve the conflict; it will merely postpone naming it.

targets.description: Lina's reuse estimate and motivation are treated as useful reported evidence without being promoted into market validation or contained support cost.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: That matters, even if it is not a market study.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Lina's judgment and motivation are evidence, but not yet evidence that the remaining thirty percent—or the support expectations around it—will stay contained.

targets.description: The no-production-code boundary and the possibility that Northline hears a polite refusal remain unresolved inside the provisional plan.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I still worry that “no production code” wastes Lina's best way of learning and that Northline will hear a polite no.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Neither step guarantees trust or a good product decision, but both make misunderstanding easier to notice before momentum chooses for you.

targets.description: The user challenges the assistant's loud-customer framing; the assistant accepts the correction and broadens the frame to relationship obligation plus product learning.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I think you are making them sound louder and more demanding than they are.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Fair correction.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Their request may be both a relationship obligation and a legitimate product lead.

targets.description: The user reaches a conditional four-month program direction with coordinator, curriculum, and review conditions, while readiness remains unresolved.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I am leaning toward accepting a four-month, twice-monthly program at Willow Hub, but only if we recruit one named site coordinator and finish the first version of the drop-in curriculum before launch.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: That is a conditional direction, not a disguised final answer, and the unresolved point matters.

targets.description: Recruiting volunteers into named roles before launch is considered as a test of capacity without assuming all required ownership will appear.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: You could test that assumption directly: recruit for named roles at the second site before announcing a launch.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: If the energy is real, it should translate into some concrete ownership, though not necessarily all the ownership you need.

targets.description: An informal foundation comment is retained as weak reported evidence rather than financing or a likely grant.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: A foundation officer told me informally that geographic reach would make our next application easier to explain.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: She did not promise anything, and the current grant pays for curriculum improvement, not expansion.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Treat the foundation comment as one input, not financing.

targets.description: The program direction remains conditional because partly ready materials have no agreed treatment.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I have not decided what happens if we find the coordinator but the materials are only partly ready.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: But setting that threshold will still involve judgment, and your colleague may reasonably challenge it.

targets.description: The user challenges stable attendance as an exclusionary standard; the assistant accepts the correction and redefines consistency around availability and learning quality.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: You are treating the current variation as a warning sign, but some of it is normal.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: That is an important correction.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Consistency in this setting may need to describe the program's availability and learning quality, not the same people attending every week.

targets.description: The user moves from demanding a major re-edit toward listening to the revised cut before deciding and proposes equal top-line credit with unresolved authority concerns.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: My provisional plan is to hear Jonah's revised cut before deciding about postponement.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The revised cut could resolve the edit question and leave the partnership question open.

targets.description: The pair considers comparing approved and current cuts before asking the participant, with a limited consent question only if they remain split.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: You could first compare the approved cut and current ending yourselves, describe the interpretive change without arguing motives, and decide whether it crosses the scope of what she approved.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: If you cannot agree, a limited factual or consent question may be better than asking her to adjudicate your artistic conflict.

targets.description: The curator's reaction is kept as evidence of dramatic force but not evidence that the representation is fair.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: A curator from the showcase listened yesterday.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The curator's response is useful evidence about the ending's force, not evidence that its interpretation is fair.

targets.description: Credit may acknowledge the completed work while authority conflict remains unresolved for the partnership and future collaboration.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I want to separate the current film from the rules for our next collaboration, and I am not sure they can really be separated.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: You do not need to solve the next project before the showcase, but you may need to avoid using a harmonious credit line as evidence that the underlying process felt mutual.

targets.description: The user challenges the assistant for moving too quickly to one side; the assistant accepts the correction and replaces automatic participant contact with an internal comparison-first sequence.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: You moved very quickly to my side.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: That is fair.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Contacting her is not automatically the respectful option.

targets.description: The user reaches a fixed-window workshop-preview direction instead of an immediate public beta, while accepting that the temporary label cannot control all downstream use.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I am leaning toward releasing an openly downloadable “workshop preview” with a fixed end date, office hours, and no compatibility promise, then deciding on the public beta after we review installation failures and the maintainer returns.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The plan can bound your promise; it cannot make public use temporary in every practical sense.

targets.description: A bounded installation test is considered as an alternative to both full beta and internal polishing, while repeated studies risk recreating endless preview.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: A bounded installation test with people who lack staff engineering might answer that question faster than either a full beta or more internal polishing.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Still, if every uncertainty becomes a separate pre-release study, you recreate the endless preview problem you already identified.

targets.description: Private-lab smoothness is downgraded after discovering hidden staff-engineer support and is not treated as representative release evidence.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Their researchers reported a smooth experience because they never saw the setup work.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: It argues against treating the private labs as representative, but it does not choose the next step by itself.

targets.description: Citation remains an unresolved durability commitment that a temporary preview label cannot fully contain.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I have not resolved whether citations should be allowed to reference the preview.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Citation is the unresolved commitment because it can turn a temporary preview into a durable scholarly object.

targets.description: The user challenges indefinite structured preview; the assistant accepts that non-release is itself a product choice and reframes the issue around support promises.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: That is close to what the maintainers say, but the structured preview has been “one more cohort” for six months.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Agreed—indefinite preview is itself a product choice, and it can narrow both the community and the evidence you receive.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The question may be less “is it ready?” than “what support promise accompanies the release, and can the team sustain that promise?”

targets.description: The user moves toward accepting a narrow exhibition with joint display support and participatory captions while preserving the unresolved object-selection rule.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I am leaning toward accepting the slot, choosing a narrow theme about the family's first ten years in the neighborhood, and limiting the exhibition to material that Tomas and I both support displaying.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: The direction is narrower and more participatory, but the decision rule is still the heart of it.

targets.description: A narrow exhibition about how memory is assembled is considered but may displace the family lives and migration story Tomas values.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: You could define the exhibition more narrowly—as twenty objects about how family memory is assembled—rather than as a representative family history.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: That may be honest, though it risks making the process the subject when Tomas wants the lives and migration stories to remain central.

targets.description: The user distinguishes Tomas's general argument from a threatened action; the assistant preserves that principle/action boundary.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: Tomas says one person's discomfort should not control a shared history, but he has not said he would use it without permission.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: It is useful to separate the principle he is testing from the action he intends.

targets.description: The meaning of mutual support for a disputed essential object remains unresolved and may be prematurely hardened by the deadline.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I have not decided what “both support” means if Tomas thinks a disputed object is essential and I think the dispute itself makes it unsuitable.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I also worry a one-month commitment will make that unresolved rule feel settled.

targets.description: The user challenges the assistant's implication that Tomas wants cosmetic resolution; the assistant reframes the conflict as different tolerances for incomplete evidence.

source_evidence.speaker: user
source_evidence.quote: I do not think Tomas wants to resolve it cosmetically.

source_evidence.speaker: assistant
source_evidence.quote: Then the difference may be less honesty versus polish and more tolerance for incomplete evidence.
